title: Convergence Analysis of the Quantum Blahut-Arimoto Algorithm and the Contraction Coefficient of Qubit Amplitude-Damping Channels
abstract: In this work, we investigate the convergence rate of the quantum Blahut-Arimoto (BA) algorithm proposed for computing the coherent information of less noisy quantum channels. Previous work established exponential convergence under certain restrictive assumptions on the channel. Using a Taylor expansion around a positive definite optimizer, we show that, for an injective degradable channel whose degrading channel has a relative-entropy contraction coefficient strictly less than one, the algorithm converges at an exponential rate after sufficiently many iterations. We further verify this condition for qubit amplitude-damping (AD) channels in the relevant parameter regime.   In addition, by analyzing the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori (BKM) metric on the Bloch ball, we derive an explicit characterization of the relative-entropy contraction coefficient of qubit AD channels. The proposed approach is further extended to calculate the relative contraction coefficient and the relative expansion coefficient of two qubit AD channels.
summary: This work analyzes the convergence properties of the quantum Blahut-Arimoto algorithm, a tool for calculating quantum channel capacities. By employing the BKM metric, the authors establish that convergence is governed by the relative-entropy contraction coefficient. They apply this theory to the qubit amplitude-damping channel, providing an explicit mathematical characterization of this key contraction parameter.
main_problem: The paper investigates the convergence rate of the quantum Blahut-Arimoto (BA) algorithm and derives an explicit characterization of the relative-entropy contraction coefficient for quantum channels.
main_result: It proves that the quantum BA algorithm converges exponentially for injective degradable channels under a condition related to the relative-entropy contraction coefficient being less than one. This coefficient is explicitly characterized for qubit amplitude-damping channels.
method: The analysis employs Taylor expansion around the optimizer and utilizes the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori (BKM) metric on the Bloch ball to analyze the local geometry of the quantum relative entropy.
model_or_system: The study focuses on general quantum channels, with a specific, detailed analysis performed on the qubit amplitude-damping (AD) channel, which models energy relaxation in qubits.
key_observables: Coherent information ($I_{	ext{coh}}$), relative-entropy contraction coefficient ($\eta(\Phi)$), and the BKM metric coefficients.
important_parameters: The contraction coefficient $\eta(\Phi)$ must be strictly less than one for guaranteed exponential convergence.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the channel being degradable and uses local quadratic bounds derived from the Taylor expansion of the relative entropy divergence.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the analysis involves deriving ratios of second derivatives ($\Gamma(u)$) and proving matrix inequalities ($K \ge 0$) related to the channel structure.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the convergence criteria using the BKM metric, then applies this framework to derive explicit formulas for the relative contraction coefficients of the AD channel, culminating in detailed mathematical proofs involving functional inequalities.
why_interesting: The rigorous characterization of channel contraction coefficients using geometric tools like the BKM metric provides deep insights into the stability and information-theoretic limits of open quantum systems, which is crucial for quantum communication protocols.
